stem.text: Figure 8.1 shows three processes that require energy in living organisms.

stem.caption: Figure 8.1
stem.alt: Three energy-requiring processes labelled A, B and C.

stem.text: State the name of each type of process shown in A, B and C.

points.text: B = anabolism / anabolic (reaction) / polymerisation / bond formation / condensation (reaction) ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: Classify the change represented, rather than naming the whole pathway in which it occurs. Moving a substance against its concentration gradient, making bonds between monomers and raising chlorophyll electrons to a higher energy level are different energy transfers.

reasoningChain: Follow the direction of movement or the structural change in each panel.
Name the specific process represented by A, B and C.

stem.text: ATP is produced in mitochondria by a process called chemiosmosis.
Outline the process of chemiosmosis in mitochondria.

points.text: protons are pumped into intermembrane space / proton gradient formed / ADP + inorganic phosphate ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: The inner mitochondrial membrane separates compartments with different proton concentrations. ATP synthase couples the energetically favourable return of protons to the phosphorylation of ADP.

reasoningChain: Identify the proton gradient across the inner membrane.
Connect proton return through ATP synthase to ATP formation.

stem.text: Different respiratory substrates have different energy values.
Table 8.1 shows the approximate energy values of carbohydrate and lipid.
Calculate the mass of carbohydrate needed to release the same quantity of energy as 100 g of lipid.
Give your answer to one decimal place.

guidance:
allow 1 mark for:
[37.8 / 17.0] ×100
or
not to one decimal place

explanation.text: Use energy values to put both substrates on the same basis: 100 g of lipid releases 3780 kJ, so divide 3780 kJ by the carbohydrate value of 17.0 kJ g<sup>−1</sup>.

reasoningChain: Calculate the energy released by 100 g of lipid.
Divide by carbohydrate energy per gram and round only the final mass to one decimal place.

issues.note: 原 MS 用方括号包围上下排列的 37.8/17.0 分式，括号右侧为 ×100。浏览器复核发现 Unicode 括号拼片会错位，现保留方括号、原数字和乘号，用 / 表示同一分式，待人工审核。原 QP 的答题线末尾还有单位 g；现有 answerLines 仅支持线前标签，未能在末尾显示该单位，此显示限制仍待处理。
